chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about *al-salam* (advance payment for goods) regarding animals, so he said: 'Known ages and counted numbers until a known term, there is no problem with it.'

key_terms.أَسْنَانٌ: Ages (referring to the age of the animals)
key_terms.السَّلَمِ: Salam (a type of forward sale where payment is made in advance for specified goods)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid salam contract on animals in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the *salam* contract for livestock by requiring precise specification of age (*asan*), quantity (*asan*), and a fixed delivery term (*ajal*), ensuring the removal of *gharar* (uncertainty). This ruling, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on clarity in commercial transactions to protect parties from dispute, aligning with the broader Islamic legal principle that advance payment sales are permissible provided the subject matter is fully defined and deliverable.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama’at who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the submission of the advance payment regarding the animals, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The age must be defined along with the numbers which must be specified for the given time, there is no problem with it’’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “

Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about advance payment to buy animals. He (the Imam) said, ‘The age must be clearly known and the numbers must be made known for the known time, then it is not unlawful.’”
